_what_this_is: What Tri-AI means by 'made for its subject'. Every value below is the shipped default, written out so it can be argued with. Delete the file and nothing changes; edit a value and every task from the next one onward is held to it. A typo here is logged and ignored, never fatal.
_how_it_works: For any request to MAKE something a person looks at, the agent is told to use its web tools first, find real examples in that field, and write BRIEF.md - palette, type, layout, and a 'Must appear' list of concrete strings those real examples carry. The verifier then holds the finished file to that list. The agent sets its own bar by going and looking; this file only says how high the bar has to be.
_min_references: How many real examples the agent must look at before it writes anything.
_min_must_appear: How many concrete, literal strings the brief must promise. Units, pack sizes, prices with their currency symbol, certifications, place names, terms of the trade. Not adjectives.
_min_palette: Distinct hex colours that must appear in the finished file.
_require_typeface: A real typeface, loaded from fonts.googleapis.com or an @font-face rule. The page the user rejected used the framework's default system stack and nothing else.
_require_imagery: An img, svg, picture or background-image somewhere. A wall of text is not a designed page.
_max_generic_headings: How many of the headings below may appear before the page is just a business template. One is ordinary; the set is the tell.
_banned_phrases: Matched literally against the visible text, case-folded. Each is a phrase someone writing about their own product would not reach for. Add your own; an empty list is ignored rather than obeyed, so a check cannot be disarmed by accident.
_visual_markers: Words that mean the request produces something to look at. A request needs one of these AND a making verb, so 'fix the spacing in report.html' stays a repair and does not trigger a redesign.
